report_review.summary: Overall, daycare observations provide mixed evidence across the ASD DSM-5 exemplar criteria. A1 and A2 show insufficient cross-context evidence; A3 shows peer-interaction concerns in daycare; B1 and B4 show clear behavioral and sensory patterns in the daycare setting; B2 shows distress with transitions. B3 lacks clear, cross-context evidence of highly restricted interests. Home context is limited or unknown for many items, limiting broader conclusions. The referenced Carpenter (2013) exemplars were consulted for criterion framing, but this dataset remains a pre-publication exemplar set and not a definitive diagnostic tool.
strengths: Observes responsive behavior to name in daycare (indication of social responsiveness)
Eye contact and social smiling observed in daycare contexts (positive social responsiveness indicators)
Child demonstrates imitation abilities (question 15; observed in daycare context) - supports some preserved social learning skills.
limitations: Observations are restricted to daycare contexts for most items; home environment data are incomplete or unknown
Some caregiver reports are unknown or inconclusive (e.g., Q2, Q19, Q20) limiting cross-context conclusions
B3 evidence is not clearly demonstrated in available data; home-context data would be needed to assess fixated interests across contexts
The source material is pre-publication DSM-5 exemplars and not a current diagnostic standard; require clinical assessment for diagnostic conclusions

report_review.summary: Seven DSM-5 ASD-exemplar criteria are represented in caregiver reports. A1 and A2 show deficits in social reciprocity and nonverbal communication (evidence: lack of social smile and eye contact, not showing objects, and absence of imitation). A3 indicates reduced social engagement with peers. B1 shows repetitive, nonfunctional play (lining up cars); B2 shows rigidity with routine changes; B3 shows a narrow, intense interest (spinning wheels); B4 shows sensory reactivity (noise sensitivity). Onset patterns noted by caregiver (patterns observed around 18 months) and reported functional impact at home (e.g., routine-related distress). This is screening data, not a clinical diagnosis; clinical assessment is required for formal ASD determination. Strengths and limitations pertain to the data source (caregiver report, pre-publication exemplars) and context provided.
limitations: Single-informant data; potential reporting bias; preliminary DSM-5 exemplar material (pre-publication) may not reflect current practice; not all domains observed across contexts. Statements include onset/impact context which may influence interpretation.
